888: 
889: The shared news executor is a plain internal function, not a framework API. Its exact name is an implementation detail; it must accept the path ID explicitly from its two callers. The table describes the design attachment points; current code still has separate tool/prefetch implementations and no registry.
890: 
891: Design rules:
892: 
893: - Each position has exactly one observation site. Router and vendor code do not write a second availability record.
894: - Vendor fallback attempts stay inside one business observation. Tool callbacks remain FR-02 statistics sources, not FR-03 observation sources.
895: - No global monkeypatch, middleware, dynamic proxy, or automatic inclusion of arbitrary HTTP calls or unlisted direct vendor methods.
896: - An observation represents a completed supported query result or its existing failure, not an internal HTTP request. Vendor retries/fallbacks remain inside one observation outcome.
897: - The local helper at the supported site registers the path association, executes the existing function body once with the existing arguments, classifies the final result or exception, and returns the original value or re-raises the original exception. Only an actual execution accepts a completed observation.
898: - With no active `RunContext`, the helper executes the original body directly and records nothing.
899: - Observation status is one of `available`, `no_data`, `unavailable`, `withheld`.
900: - Status recognition follows the normative per-method table in §8.3 and the narrow `DataResultClassifier`. It uses existing types, return structures, and verified producer sentinels; model text is never used, a non-empty string is not success, and an unrecognized format is `unavailable`.
901: - Existing fallback, withholding, and exception semantics are preserved.
902: - `get_news` is one method in two paths; the same business query is not split solely by call path.
903: 
904: Early failure and parameter rules:
905: 
906: - The observation boundary starts after control has entered a supported business function. Tool schema validation, an unknown tool name, or message parsing before that point is not an executed data query and receives no fabricated query observation.
907: - Existing date semantics are preserved. `as_of()` may clamp the requested date to `trade_date` or pass it through; `as_of_window()` may clamp an unreadable end or move a wholly future window back to the trade date. A request that existing logic adjusts is still executed, and the effective values actually passed onward are recorded. No stricter observation-layer validation is added.
908: - When the original body returns its date-error text before a fetch (for example an unparseable `start_date` from `as_of_window()`), record only a private `availability_call_failures` note with a fixed parameter/date category and short reason. Do not create a query key, window, `CompletedObservation`, completion sequence, or FR-01 entry. Return the original text unchanged.
909: - If the original body raises before a fetch, record the same kind of private call-failure note and propagate the original exception unchanged. Observation handling never replaces it.
910: - For P-03, date normalization happens before splitting. If it rejects the call, one private P-03 call-failure note may describe the parameter failure; no split indicator was fetched, and no per-indicator observations are fabricated. After a successful split, each indicator has its own execution and observation; the final joined string is never classified once.
911: - Effective defaults use existing code: P-10 reads `global_news_lookback_days`/`global_news_article_limit` from active config when its arguments are None; P-11 uses `DEFAULT_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (365); P-12 uses `DEFAULT_LIMIT` (6); P-14 uses limit 30; P-15 uses `limit_per_sub` 5. Do not copy a second default table or change the original call arguments.
912: - A None trade date or absent optional parameter is recorded as known-null/absent, never as an infinite window. Router paths do not infer a winning vendor from configuration; source remains known or null under the existing rule. If producers interpret a request parameter differently, record the reliable shared request semantics and the limitation, not a fabricated uniform per-vendor value.
913: - A call-failure note contains only the supported path ID/method, safe business object, fixed category such as `parameter_rejected`, short reason such as “start_date cannot be parsed,” and a fixed necessary item ID only when the path reliably maps to one. It stores no full raw arguments, arbitrary objects, payloads, configuration, or raw exception text. If the note cannot be recorded, emit an existing safe warning; do not create a fake query, do not set `availability_tracking_error` (no fetch completed), and do not alter a valid result or query mark.
914: - Completion sequence is assigned only when the registry accepts a completion update, not when the helper is entered, fetch returns, or a callback arrives. Ordinary observation, conservative unavailable observation, and query failure mark share the same lock/sequence. One shared FR-01 execution creates at most one accepted update; each real non-reuse execution creates its own. Network time, wall-clock/monotonic time, callback alignment, and distributed ordering are never used to correct acceptance order.
915: 
916: The observation helper is local and internal. It has no module-level mutable state, plugin registry, monkeypatch, middleware, or public API requirement.
917: 
918: ### 8.2 FR-01 query reuse
919: 
920: - Scope: only the `get_news` data-fetch flow reached by P-09 and P-13, for the same ticker and date window.
921: - Query key: method name plus effective business parameters after a method-specific binding of positional/keyword arguments and declared defaults. Keyword order is not semantic.
922: - Current code has the News tool and sentiment prefetch as separate date-handling/router flows. The design uses one plain internal news executor called explicitly by the News tool with P-09 and by sentiment prefetch with P-13. It performs the existing date/window handling, forms the effective ticker/window key, registers the path association, and enters single-flight. The first execution calls the router once through the local observation helper; waiters/cache hits do not observe again. No outer tool or sentiment wrapper also records that news query.
923: - If news date/window validation fails before a legal fetch key exists, the executor returns the original error text or propagates the original exception and does not create a single-flight entry. It records at most one private P-09/P-13 call-failure note with the fixed parameter/date category and short safe reason; this is not a query observation, completion sequence, or query mark. If even that note cannot be recorded, it warns. It does not invent a legal window, cache entry, or map the invalid window to an earlier valid one.
924: - No alias inference, fuzzy matching, list reordering, cross-method merge, or cross-run state.
925: - First caller starts one existing data-fetch flow; later/concurrent callers reuse its outcome.
926: - Single-flight waiters receive the value or the same failure type/reason. No production deadline/cancellation protocol is added.
927: - A mutable result is copied per consumer, or stored in an immutable/serialized form, so one consumer cannot pollute another.
928: - A reuse hit preserves the original FR-03 status, reason, and source; it does not create a new observation or completion sequence.
929: - Existing vendor caches remain and are not FR-01 reuse.
930: - `QueryReuseService` is owned by `RunContext`; no module-level global reuse state.
931: - The shared news executor receives its internal path identity explicitly from its caller. It is not inferred from the shared function name, a tool callback, the model, or process-global state. This covers both the P-09 tool call and the P-13 sentiment prefetch.
932: - Path identity does not enter the model-visible business parameters or the query key. Concurrent tasks must carry their own path identity without cross-task leakage. A narrow internal argument or a scoped binding may be used; the exact framework integration remains pending verification.
933: 
934: ### 8.3 FR-03 availability summary
935: 
936: Observation record:
937: 
938: `CompletedObservation` fields:
939: 
940: | Field | Meaning |
941: |---|---|
942: | `method` / `object` / `range` | Effective business query identity and display context |
943: | `query_key` | Method plus effective business parameters only; never a call path |
944: | `executing_path_id` | The supported path that started the shared execution; P-01–P-15 |
945: | `source` | Actual source when reliably known; otherwise unknown/null |
946: | `status` | `available` / `no_data` / `unavailable` / `withheld` |
947: | `reason` | Short safe reason |
948: | `completion_sequence` | Run-local increasing order assigned when the registry accepts a completion update |
949: 
950: Internal path-association map (conceptual only; not a persistent object):
951: 
952: | Field | Meaning |
953: |---|---|
954: | `query_key` | Same method-plus-parameters key; path is excluded |
955: | `supported_path_ids` | Supported P-01–P-15 paths that actually requested this query in this run |
956: 
957: The registry stores a simple `query_key → set of supported path_id` map. No persistence object, association ID, event log, hit counter, or history interface is added.
958: 
959: Association rules:
960: 
961: - A path association may be recorded when the supported observation site begins the query, before a completed result exists. It does not produce a completion sequence and does not change status, reason, or source.
962: - Only a path association with no completed observation is not `available`; it cannot fabricate a completed result.
963: - `executing_path_id` identifies the first caller that started the shared execution. Other requesting paths belong only in `supported_path_ids`.
964: - If the implementation retains a field named `path_id`, it is an alias for `executing_path_id` only and never represents all requesting paths.
965: - No hit-event log, call count, or query-execution statistic is added.
966: - Different objects, windows, methods, or effective parameters remain different queries; path association never merges them.
967: 
968: Classification contract:
969: 
970: `DataResultClassifier.classify(method, effective_params, raw_result_or_exception, source_hint)` returns status, short safe reason, and source. `source_hint` is supplied only by a supported site/direct producer that knows the source (a direct fetcher or single-vendor path); it is never inferred from configuration. The classifier preserves the original return or exception. It does not fetch, call a model, infer a vendor from configuration, or use generic keyword guessing. A non-empty string is never sufficient for `available`. If a result does not match a verified producer branch, the conservative status is `unavailable` with reason `unrecognized result format`; it is not marked available.
971: 
972: Composition order:
973: 
974: ```text
975: Shared news executor called with P-09 or P-13
976:   → existing parameter/date handling
977:   → query identity and actual path association
978:   → run-scoped single-flight
979:       First caller:
980:         execute the existing fetch/fallback once
981:         preserve its original value or exception

1057: Minimum-content boundaries:
1058: 
1059: - A verified snapshot with a valid price record remains `available` even when some indicators are `N/A` or `N/A (...)`; do not require every OHLCV, indicator, or valuation field.
1060: - Fundamentals with at least one recognized non-empty basic field are `available`; do not require every field or a complete profile.
1061: - Ticker/global news with at least one actual article entry are `available`; do not add article-count, relevance, truth, sufficiency, or full-period checks.
1062: - P-01 CSV with only a header has no actual data row and is not `available`. Do not extend this clarification into new CSV rules for unrelated paths.
1063: - A heading, placeholder, error text, or a number found anywhere is not sufficient for `available`.
1064: - If basic data exists and only non-critical parts are missing, remain `available`; do not convert every non-available result to `no_data`.
1065: 
1066: Unverified or conservative mappings:
1067: 
1068: - Alpha Vantage `OVERVIEW`, statement, insider, and `NEWS_SENTIMENT` empty-payload shapes are not all represented by dedicated repository fixtures. The design treats an empty JSON object, empty report array, empty `feed`, or empty insider data array as `no_data`, and malformed/non-JSON as `unavailable`; the exact producer shapes must be confirmed before implementation acceptance.
1069: - Alpha Vantage header-only stock CSV classification is derived from `_filter_csv_by_date_range` returning a header-only frame; a direct fixture is still planned.
1070: - Alpha Vantage statement JSON does not use the `freq` parameter in the current producer. The classifier uses the returned report arrays as the producer’s actual output and does not fabricate missing periods or a different frequency.
1071: - Router methods do not expose which vendor served the final result. Actual source remains unknown/null; the configured vendor chain is not used as a substitute.
1072: - `get_indicators` may concatenate multiple indicators in one tool call. Implementation must classify each requested indicator before concatenation. A whole-string non-empty check is not a valid classifier.
1073: - If a producer branch cannot be confidently classified, the observation is `unavailable` with `unrecognized result format`, not `available`.
1074: - If final text cannot reliably distinguish a branch after the table is verified, a minimal internal status hint may be passed from that producer branch. This is a future implementation option, not implemented in this round, and must not become a wholesale rewrite of all vendor responses.
1075: 
1076: `AvailabilitySummary` contract:
1077: 
1078: The summarizer returns one ordinary JSON-compatible mapping. It is the complete business summary; consumers do not add fields or rebuild completeness.
1079: 
1080: | Field | Type and content |
1081: |---|---|
1082: | `basic_completeness` | `complete` / `incomplete` / `not_applicable` |
1083: | `applicability_note` | Short explanation of non-applicability; empty string otherwise |
1084: | `observations` | One projection per current logical query: the last effective result selected by existing object/range/effective-parameter and last-completed rules, with `method`, `object`, `effective_parameters`, `executing_path_id`, `supported_path_ids`, `source`, `status` in the four-status set, and `reason` |
1085: | `necessary_items` | Applicable items for enabled analysts: fixed `item_id`, `method`, `object`, `applicable_range`, `status` in the four-status set or `not_attempted` when no completed result is available, and `reason` |
1086: | `supplementary_limitations` | Actually failed or limited supplementary items, including pre-fetch parameter/date limitations, with `method`, `object`, reliable known parameters, known source or null, `status`, and short `reason` |
1087: 
1088: Rules:
1089: 
1090: - The field contents serve only current FR-03 semantics; this is not a generic evidence model.
1091: - A query-level failure mark is projected only into the affected current query's observation as `status = unavailable` with a reason such as `availability record failed; cannot confirm`. The projection is a consumer view, not a fabricated stored `CompletedObservation`. It is not exposed as a failure-mark field, a new status, a public registry object, or a source proof.
1092: - A marked query does not reuse an earlier success. A later accepted update for the same query replaces the mark; other queries are unaffected. `necessary_items` use the selected current projection, so a marked necessary query appears unavailable with the safe failure reason.
1093: - `not_attempted` appears only in `necessary_items`, never in `observations` and never as a fake completed record. Display “no completed result available” unless the item is known not to have been invoked; only then say “not executed.”
1094: - Do not store `missing_necessary_items`. The necessary gap is the simple consumer-visible filter over the at most seven `necessary_items` entries whose status is not `available`. That filter is not a second completeness calculation.
1095: - Supplementary limitations never count as necessary gaps and do not change `basic_completeness`. A necessary-item failure is represented in `necessary_items` and is not duplicated in `supplementary_limitations`.
1096: - Different objects, windows, methods, and effective parameters remain different queries.
1097: - The mapping contains no version, hash, digest, source proof, history ledger, or independent schema file.
1098: 
1099: Completeness is computed once by the summarizer:
1100: 
1101: - Non-stock or no applicable necessary item: `not_applicable`, with `applicability_note`.
1102: - Every applicable necessary item in `necessary_items` is `available`: `complete`.
1103: - Otherwise: `incomplete`, with the corresponding non-available necessary item and reason supplying the gap. A query-level mark is already projected as that selected item's `unavailable`; completeness does not separately re-check marks. Supplementary limitations do not change this rule.
1104: 
1105: The external snapshot interface receives `asset_type`, `enabled_analysts`, and the small existing `analysis_context` needed for object/range matching as explicit arguments. `asset_type` comes from `state["asset_type"]`, populated by `Propagator.create_initial_state`: the CLI derives it from the selected ticker through `detect_asset_type()` and carries it in the selections/state, while `propagate(..., asset_type=...)` supplies the explicit existing parameter (defaulting as that API already does). No separate effective-config key or new asset detector is added. `enabled_analysts` is the existing selected-analyst set used to build the graph; the object is `state["company_of_interest"]`, the analysis date is `state["trade_date"]`, and the existing tool arguments provide any additional date/window values. The research wrapper, final-check node, and report path supply these existing values; no new configuration system is added. A `necessity_status` helper may remain internal only and is not called by consumers.
1106: 
1107: Existing-data source mapping for the seven necessary items:
1108: 
1109: | Necessary item | Object source | Date/window source | Existing direct matching |
1110: |---|---|---|---|
1111: | `get_stock_data` | `state["company_of_interest"]` | Tool `start_date`/`end_date` after existing `as_of_window(..., trade_date)` handling | Same object and effective start/end; no coverage or period inference |
1112: | `get_verified_market_snapshot` | `state["company_of_interest"]` | Existing tool `curr_date` after `as_of(..., trade_date)`, plus `look_back_days` | Same object and analysis/effective date; utility lookback does not create a new necessity dimension |
1113: | `get_income_statement` | `state["company_of_interest"]` | Existing `freq` (default `quarterly`) and `as_of(curr_date, trade_date)` | Existing interface semantics; no annual/quarter substitution or missing-period inference |
1114: | `get_balance_sheet` | `state["company_of_interest"]` | Existing `freq` (default `quarterly`) and `as_of(curr_date, trade_date)` | Existing interface semantics; no annual/quarter substitution or missing-period inference |
1115: | `get_cashflow` | `state["company_of_interest"]` | Existing `freq` (default `quarterly`) and `as_of(curr_date, trade_date)` | Existing interface semantics; no annual/quarter substitution or missing-period inference |
1116: | `get_global_news` | Global news item; no ticker object | Existing analysis date plus `as_of(...)` and configured `global_news_lookback_days`/`global_news_article_limit` defaults | Current analysis date/window; it does not stand in for ticker-news availability |
1117: | `fetch_reddit_posts` | `state["company_of_interest"]` | Existing sentiment prefetch window from `_seven_days_back(trade_date)` through `trade_date`; `subreddits_for(ticker)`; `limit_per_sub` default 5 | Same object and prefetch window; StockTwits does not substitute for the Reddit item |
1118: 
1119: These rows describe existing sources and matching only. They do not add an asset-identification rule, parameter registry, range-coverage algorithm, or forced query. Target matching happens before the existing last-accepted-result selection; an available query from another object, window, or data item does not substitute for the necessary target.
1120: 
1121: For `get_verified_market_snapshot`, `get_global_news`, and `fetch_reddit_posts`, the existing entry/tool context above uniquely determines the target date/window. For `get_stock_data` and the three statement items, one analysis may issue multiple ranges or frequencies; current D1/D2 do not name which actual request is the canonical necessity target. That target-choice detail remains pending at C-07/IF-06 and must not be resolved here by inventing a default, period slot, or coverage rule. If a future entry supplies an asset type not produced by the existing `stock`/`crypto` paths, its matching is likewise unconfirmed rather than assumed to be non-stock.
1122: 
1123: Summary rules:
1124: 
1125: - The summary is run-scoped, produced by `AvailabilitySummarizer` from a read-only registry copy, and returned as an independent plain mapping. The mutable registry is not exposed.
1126: - Each accepted update receives the run-local increasing sequence under the registry lock. Concurrent work is ordered by acceptance, not network/wall/monotonic time.
1127: - The summary uses the state from the last accepted update per query as of the snapshot time. Later accepted success replaces earlier accepted failure and vice versa; success is never selected preferentially.
1128: - A query-level failure mark is a local unresolved-query condition, not a fifth status. It is an accepted update in the same sequence. While it is the latest update, an earlier observation for that query does not prove current availability; the decision view states that availability cannot be confirmed. A later accepted update for that query replaces the mark.
1129: - Different windows are retained separately. A necessity item matches the same object and the analysis's applicable range without complex coverage inference.
1130: - An item with no completed result is `not_attempted` in the decision view; it is never fabricated as an execution record or call count. Display it as “no completed result available” unless the item is known not to have been invoked; only then use “not executed”. An in-flight query is not relabeled as never started or successful.
1131: - The seven necessity items are the union for enabled analysts; disabling an analyst removes its item:
1132:   1. `get_stock_data` for the current object and requested range.
1133:   2. `get_verified_market_snapshot` for the current object and analysis date.
1134:   3. `get_income_statement` under existing interface semantics.
1135:   4. `get_balance_sheet` under existing interface semantics.
1136:   5. `get_cashflow` under existing interface semantics.
1137:   6. `get_global_news` for the current news-analysis range.
1138:   7. `fetch_reddit_posts` for the current object and prefetch window.
1139: - Basic completeness: `complete` only when every applicable `necessary_items` entry is `available`; `incomplete` when any applicable entry is `no_data`, `unavailable`, `withheld`, or has no completed result; `not_applicable` when no item applies or the asset is outside stock scope. A query-level mark is already projected into its selected item as `unavailable`, so there is no second mark check. A withheld necessity item does not bypass completeness. A marked supplementary query is disclosed as a limitation but does not by itself change basic completeness.
1140: - Supplementary data (indicators, profile/fundamentals overview, insider transactions, ticker news, FRED, prediction markets, StockTwits) is disclosed when it actually fails; an unqueried supplementary item is not reported item by item.
1141: - Global news does not represent ticker-news availability; ticker-news unavailability is disclosed separately. StockTwits success does not substitute for the Reddit necessity item.
1142: - No forced fetch, automatic refetch, retry, or model re-run on summary refresh.
1143: - A snapshot returns `None` when `availability_tracking_error` is set or when that snapshot construction fails. With the tracking error, later snapshots remain `None`; with only a construction failure, a later call may reconstruct from intact records. A missing snapshot follows SB-01's existing missing/invalid-summary handling. Neither case fabricates a completeness value or adds a business gate; the tracking error is not the withdrawn public `summary_confirmable` state.
1144: - FR-03 does not write a formal rating or create a new gate condition.
1145: - Consumers:
1146:   - Research stage: the wrapper obtains one summary at research start, renders its program block for the first Bull call, and stores it as `research_availability_summary`. Later Bull/Bear rounds and the Research Manager read that same mapping; they do not refresh, re-aggregate queries, or infer availability from model text.
1147:   - Final check: takes its own current summary and reads `basic_completeness`, `necessary_items`, `applicability_note`, and the necessary-item reasons. It does not read the registry or failure marks and does not recompute completeness.
1148:   - Report: the entry prepares one terminal summary from this run's registry after graph execution and before save/return, and places it in `data_availability_summary` of the report-state/final-state mapping. The writer deterministically displays basic completeness, necessary gaps (by filtering non-available necessary items), and supplementary limitations from that mapping. The writer never obtains a new snapshot. If no valid summary exists, that region says the program summary is unavailable; it does not invent a fourth completeness state. The model cannot overwrite that region.
1149:   - CLI deterministic risk/availability display uses the same prepared final-state summary fields and does not reconstruct the summary; when none exists it says the program summary is unavailable. Showing a previously generated file uses that file's data.
1150:   - Consumers at the same time receive identical content; different-time summaries may differ.
1151: - The deterministic display text is program-generated; model output cannot rewrite structured records or the deterministic availability region.
1152: - A consumer may filter `necessary_items` to find non-available gaps for display or basic contradiction checks; it must not recompute `basic_completeness` or invent another gap list.
1153: - FR-03 does not require FR-01 to be enabled. It records actual query results without a query cache and may reuse the query-identity rule; an FR-01 hit preserves the original status, reason, and source.
1154: 
1155: #### Research-stage summary attachment
1156: 
1157: “Research start” is the analyst join immediately before the first Bull Researcher call, not the start of the Research Manager.
1158: 
1159: ```text
1160: Analyst join
1161:   → First research-entry preparation (wrapper around the first Bull call, not a top-level node)
1162:       → snapshot current-run AvailabilityRegistry
1163:       → render a labeled program block deterministically
1164:       → inject it into the same first Bull invocation
1165:       → store research_availability_summary in graph state
1166:   → Bull/Bear debate
1167:   → Research Manager
1168: ```
1169: 
1170: Contract:
1171: 
1172: - `research_availability_summary` is either the independent JSON-compatible summary mapping as of research start or `null` when none can be formed. The “program summary currently unavailable” text exists only in deterministic rendering, not as a stored third type.
1173: - `null` is not a fourth `basic_completeness` value and does not fabricate a summary. The original analysis materials remain available.
1174: - A small deterministic rendering function produces a clearly labeled program content block. It does not call a model or data source, compress, or truncate.
1175: - The first Bull call receives the rendered block directly. Returning a state update and assuming the current function can read it is not sufficient.
1176: - Subsequent Bull/Bear rounds and the Research Manager read `research_availability_summary` directly from graph state and include the same stage summary as an explicit program block in their prompts.
1177: - The model cannot rewrite structured fields or the deterministic program block. The program summary is not mixed with model-generated analysis as one authority source.
1178: - The full analyst reports remain; the summary is additive and does not replace the reports with briefs.
1179: - Preparation runs only on the first entry to the research stage. A later Bull/Bear round or debate loop does not refresh it.
1180: - Later observations do not rewrite this stage input and do not re-run research.
1181: - The post-PM final check takes its own check-time snapshot. After the formal check, the entry prepares the terminal report/delivery summary from the same run's registry; the report writer itself does not take a snapshot. Neither overwrites the research-stage input. The final program check reads program state, not model prose.
1182: - No new data request, model call, seal, versioned view, or second completeness authority is added.
1183: 
1184: Checkpoint interaction:
1185: 
1186: - The new flow always executes research from its normal entry and never resumes a checkpoint. A checkpoint-enabled configuration only emits the no-resume notice; old checkpoint material is not used as current research or final-check evidence.
1187: 
1188: ### 8.4 FR-04 purchase risk
1189: 
1190: Input transport:
1191: 
1192: - Optional `purchase_scenario` keyword for `propagate()` and optional CLI `--purchase-scenario <json-file>`.
1193: - An explicitly provided scenario file that cannot be read or parsed is a caller parameter error before run creation (or a controlled setup error). A file that is not provided is distinct from that failure: the absence is passed to FR-04, and an applicable stock Buy/Overweight then gets structured `blocked` without an entry hard failure.
1194: - After successful input acquisition, business-invalid fields, a mismatched object/ticker, or an invalid explicit threshold are FR-04 results, not entry pre-validation hard failures.
1195: - The evaluator receives the current analysis ticker explicitly. It does not read a global, parse a report, or infer the ticker from the scenario.
1196: - The existing `PortfolioContext` is not a source for scenario fields. `average_price`, model text, and network lookup are never used to fill a missing scenario value.
1197: 
1198: Scenario and threshold contract:
1199: 
1200: | Field | Constraint |
1201: |---|---|
1202: | `ticker` | Matches the analysis ticker under existing pure ticker normalization (`normalize_symbol`); no network identity lookup |
1203: | `portfolio_value` | Finite decimal, greater than zero |
1204: | `current_position_value` | Finite decimal, between zero and `portfolio_value` inclusive |
1205: | `proposed_buy_value` | Finite decimal, greater than zero |
1206: | `entry_price` | Finite decimal, greater than zero |
1207: | `stop_loss_price` | Finite decimal, greater than zero and less than `entry_price` |
1208: | `currency` | Non-empty common currency label for the amounts and prices |
1209: | `max_projected_weight` | Finite decimal, greater than zero and at most one |
1210: | `max_stop_distance` | Finite decimal, greater than zero and less than one |
1211: 
1212: Common rules:
1213: 
1214: - Reject booleans, NaN, Infinity, missing values, and unparseable values.
1215: - Accept ordinary decimal notation. No special length, trailing-zero, or canonical-grammar requirement is added.
1216: - Use `0.30` / `0.05` only when the threshold is omitted. An explicitly invalid threshold is blocked and never falls back to a default.
1217: - Do not add cash sufficiency, fees, slippage, marketability, liveness, account truth, account completeness, currency conversion, order execution, or order-type checks. No additional scenario fields such as cash, quantity, `valuation_price`, `valuation_time`, `candidate_id`, `order_count`, or provenance are required or added. The structure remains one stock, one unlevered purchase/add-long; no derivative, leverage, or multiple-order model is added.
1218: - A mismatched ticker, each invalid field, or an invalid threshold produces `blocked` and names the field or configuration category; no unhandled divide-by-zero or numeric error escapes.
1219: - The thresholds are classroom demonstration defaults, not approved financial policy. Every result states this.
1220: 
1221: Judgment order:
1222: 
1223: 1. Legal model rating check.
1224: 2. Asset/rating applicability.
1225: 3. Applicable scenario and threshold validation.
1226: 4. Legal metric calculation and comparison.
1227: 5. Structured result.
1228: 
1229: Applicability:
1230: 
1231: | Case | Result |
1232: |---|---|
1233: | Stock + Buy/Overweight with a valid scenario | Evaluate both rules |
1234: | Stock + Buy/Overweight with missing or invalid scenario | `blocked`; never `not_applicable` |
1235: | Stock + Hold/Underweight/Sell | `not_applicable` |
1236: | Non-stock asset + legal rating | `not_applicable`; stock scenario rules are not used |
1237: | Missing or illegal rating | `blocked`; not disguised as non-applicability |
1238: | Unexpected evaluator exception | `error`; never `passed` |
1239: 
1240: Numeric handling and exact decision:
1241: 
1242: - **Evaluator internal representation**: legal decimal values are parsed into an exact numeric representation. Use a standard-library exact rational value (for example, `fractions.Fraction`) for the pass/block arithmetic; do not depend on the ambient `Decimal` context.
1243: - **Decision arithmetic**: after type, finiteness, and business-range validation, convert each legal decimal exactly to an exact rational, then perform exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, and comparison:
1244:   - `current_position_value + proposed_buy_value <= max_projected_weight * portfolio_value`
1245:   - `entry_price - stop_loss_price <= max_stop_distance * entry_price`
1246: - Exact rational operations, not default `Decimal` precision, guarantee the cross-multiplication comparison. Do not globally change the Decimal context.
1247: - Equality passes. Exceeding either threshold blocks; when both exceed, both reasons are retained.
1248: - **Scenario/threshold handling**: do not require all raw inputs to be first projected into a persistent normalized state and then parsed back. Perform the necessary conversion at the actual entry and risk-module boundary. If the scenario must be carried in graph state, use a simple JSON-compatible mapping; it is not a new normalization protocol, representation version, digest, or round-trip contract.
1249: - **Result representation**: the risk result is a JSON-compatible object. `scenario` and `thresholds` are display-safe values, `projected_weight` and `stop_distance` are decimal strings or `null`, and `reasons` is a short safe string list. Do not place `Decimal` or `Fraction` objects in the result or graph state, and do not rely on an implicit universal encoder. The new flow does not use checkpoint state.
1250: - **Serialization discipline**: do not use `json.dump(default=str)` or another implicit encoder for risk objects, do not uniformly convert to float, and do not re-decide risk from formatted percentages.
1251: - **Report metrics**: `projected_weight` and `stop_distance` are computed separately from the exact decision. A repeating quotient remains computable and is not `null`. A small local formatting function may choose display precision; fixed decimal places, round-half-even, no-exponent notation, and trailing-zero rules are implementation choices, not architecture acceptance requirements or separate human-approval gates.
1252: - **Display separation**: display rounding happens after the exact decision and never feeds back into the comparison or status. CLI and report consume the same risk result but may differ in normal layout or percentage presentation; character-for-character equality is not required.
1253: - **Invalid raw input**: do not stringify an arbitrary invalid original value. The display-safe scenario omits unsafe/invalid raw values; metrics are null only by their own operand rule; valid thresholds are the only thresholds shown as used.
1254: 
1255: Input handling:
1256: 
1257: | Input | Handling |
1258: |---|---|
1259: | JSON numeric token | Parse directly into a decimal value from the token, without a binary-float intermediate |
1260: | Decimal string | Parse through the same local numeric parser |
1261: | `Decimal` | Check finiteness, then reuse the same parser and convert exactly |
1262: | Integer | Exclude bool first, then accept exactly |
1263: | Finite float | Interpret its stable decimal string representation as the supplied value; do not use float arithmetic; the system validates the converted decimal value and cannot restore precision already lost in the caller’s float computation |
1264: | Bool, NaN, Infinity | Reject |
1265: 
1266: The program interface supports ordinary numbers and decimal strings; `Decimal` can use the same parser. This is not a promise of complete equivalence among arbitrary Python numeric objects. The input and result contracts also do not add special length, trailing-zero, or canonical-grammar limits.
1267: 
1268: For the cross-multiplication comparison, the relevant denominator is a legal positive value under the scenario contract; no additional exception or special-case protocol is introduced.
1269: 
1270: Current-code evidence:
1271: 
1272: - `_log_state()` currently constructs explicit fields and does not yet persist `portfolio_risk_result` (`trading_graph.py:437-475`, ordinary `json.dump`). This is a new type-contract gap in the design, not a claim that the current code already fails to save a Decimal risk result.
1273: 
1274: Metric nullability:
1275: 
1276: - `projected_weight` is non-null only when `portfolio_value`, `current_position_value`, and `proposed_buy_value` have legal arithmetic values and the division is defined. A repeating quotient remains non-null and is formatted only for display.
1277: - `stop_distance` is non-null only when `entry_price` and `stop_loss_price` have legal arithmetic values and the division is defined. A repeating quotient remains non-null and is formatted only for display.
1278: - An invalid ticker, currency, or threshold does not by itself null a metric whose arithmetic operands are legal.
1279: - Never compute a metric from invalid operands, and never clear every metric merely because a non-arithmetic field is invalid.
1280: 
1281: Result fields:
1282: 
1283: | Field | Meaning |
1284: |---|---|
1285: | `status` | `passed` / `blocked` / `not_applicable` / `error` |
1286: | `analysis_ticker` | The current analysis ticker used for matching |
1287: | `scenario` | Display-safe actually parsable scenario input with numeric values as decimal strings; unsafe/invalid raw values are omitted |
1288: | `thresholds` | Valid thresholds actually used as decimal strings, with the classroom-demonstration note; an invalid explicit threshold is not shown as a valid default |
1289: | `projected_weight` | Decimal string or null; display precision is a local implementation choice |
1290: | `stop_distance` | Decimal string or null; display precision is a local implementation choice |
1291: | `reasons` | Short safe risk-scoped reason list naming the field or configuration category |
1292: 
1293: Consumers:
1294: 
1295: - CLI deterministic risk section.
1296: - `final_state` as `portfolio_risk_result`.
1297: - Generated report deterministic section that the model does not rewrite.
1298: - SB-01 consumes the applicable risk status and any necessary explanation from the same result; it does not recompute or re-parse the metrics. It does not reuse the risk reasons by reference or flatten the risk object into the formal fields.
1299: - CLI and report read the same risk result. They do not re-judge risk; normal layout and percentage-display differences are allowed, and character-for-character equality is not required.
1300: - The deterministic risk area states: “Only the listed caller scenario is checked; other amounts and prices in the model proposal are not verified by this check.” It also keeps the classroom-demonstration and non-trade-authorization statements.
1301: - The check uses only the amounts and prices explicitly supplied in the caller scenario. A different set of numbers in the model proposal is not automatically included, compared, or shown as verified, and does not become a new blocked condition or change the model conclusion.
1302: - The manifest does not add risk fields. The existing final-state log is not required to add a complete risk archive; memory is not required to store risk metadata.
1303: - Serialization requirements do not change existing save-failure handling or checkpoint policy.
1304: - `passed` means only that the supplied scenario meets the two checks; it is not a trade authorization.
1305: 
1306: The evaluator must not hard-fail the analysis entry merely because the scenario is missing or business-invalid; it returns a structured `blocked` result. FR-04 does not change the model rating or write formal result fields. Unrelated existing analysis exceptions keep their original behavior.
1307: 
1308: ### 8.5 SB-01 final check
1309: 
1310: Inputs: `model_proposal`, `data_availability_summary` from the risk-node check time, `portfolio_risk_result`, asset type. The later terminal delivery summary does not rerun this check.
1311: 
1312: Top-level output fields:
1313: 
1314: | Field | Type and rule |
1315: |---|---|
1316: | `model_proposal` | Nested `{rating, text}` or `null`; each inner value is `rating`/`text` or `null`; no `present` boolean |
1317: | `gate_status` | `passed`, `blocked`, or `error` |
1318: | `reasons` | Top-level SB-01 string list; passed may be empty; blocked/error has at least one actual reason; no reason code/priority system |
1319: | `final_rating` | Five-tier legal rating on passed; REVIEW on blocked/error |
1320: | `final_trade_decision` | Non-whitespace formal conclusion; program-generated manual-review notice on blocked/error |
1321: 
1322: Rules:
1323: 
1324: - Legal ratings: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell.
1325: - Missing/illegal model rating or model REVIEW: blocked, final REVIEW, with a top-level reason.
1326: - Model conclusion: it must be a non-whitespace string. Missing, wrong-type, empty-string, and whitespace-only conclusions are ordinary input-condition failures: blocked, final REVIEW, with a program-generated manual-review notice stating the actual reason. They are not handled as SB-01 internal errors. The check may test non-emptiness after stripping surrounding whitespace but must preserve the original valid conclusion unchanged on pass; it does not trim, rewrite, regenerate, or add length/format/quality/factual scoring.
1327: - FR-03 summary read: use only `basic_completeness`, `necessary_items`, and `applicability_note`, plus necessary-item reasons. `complete` passes; `incomplete` blocks with the non-available necessary items and reasons; `not_applicable` does not alone block and keeps the note.
1328: - Summary validation is limited to required field types and legal states. A complete result containing a non-available necessary item is a basic contradiction; an incomplete result with no non-available necessary item or corresponding reason is also a basic contradiction. A missing or invalid summary uses the existing missing/invalid-summary rule. No raw payload, source proof, hash, full-query audit, or new schema gate is checked.
1329: - Supplementary-data limitations are disclosed but do not separately trigger REVIEW and are not necessary gaps.
1330: - FR-04: for stock Buy/Overweight, only `passed` satisfies the risk condition. `blocked`, `error`, missing, illegal, or wrongly `not_applicable` blocks. Other legal stock ratings and legal non-stock ratings do not require the stock scenario check.
1331: - No model text substitution; no FR-04 re-call/re-implementation; no cash/freshness/policy/digest rules.
1332: - SB-01 consumes only the provided summary and risk status. It does not read the registry or query-level failure marks, re-aggregate queries, or change the formal rating from an observation-handling event.
1333: - On passed: formal rating and decision keep the proposal values; not a trade authorization. `reasons` may be empty and no pass reason is invented.
1334: - On blocked/error: `final_rating = REVIEW`; `final_trade_decision` is a program-generated manual-review notice with actual reasons; top-level `reasons` explains why.
1335: - Risk reasons remain in `portfolio_risk_result.reasons`; SB-01 writes its own top-level `reasons` without flattening or overwriting the risk object.
1336: - `model_proposal` remains separately labeled; never the formal conclusion.
1337: - The node catches unexpected internal errors and returns `error`/REVIEW with an actual top-level reason; it does not raise a substitute analysis failure.
1338: 
1339: ### 8.6 FR-05 history read
1340: 
1341: Interface:
1342: 
1343: - `list_runs(ticker=None, analysis_date=None) -> list[RunSummary]`.
1344: - `get_report(run_id) -> str`.
1345: 
1346: Registration:
1347: 
1348: - The FR-02 manifest is the only registration source.
1349: - A record enters history only when a parseable, supported-format `completed` manifest registers a merged Markdown report reference. A normal `report: null` is a legal no-report record, not a corrupt one, and does not enter the list.
1350: - Running/failed records, legal no-report records, and unregistered report files are not guaranteed to appear. A missing required `report` key is format damage; list skips it with a safe warning and direct get treats it as an invalid record.

1429: ## 9. Security and permissions
1430: 
1431: ### 9.1 SR-01 credential protection
1432: 
1433: Supported scope only:
1434: 
1435: 1. FR-02 manifest configuration and error summaries.
1436: 2. Existing report and final-state configuration summaries.
1437: 3. CLI endpoint preference save/load.
1438: 4. Existing `get_scrubbed()` request-error paths in `dataflows/net.py`, Alpha Vantage `common.py` and its notice helper, and FRED `fred.py` including the passthrough 400 `error_message` path.
1439: 5. Warnings from these handlers.
1440: 
1441: Rules:
1442: 
1443: - Configuration summary reuses `run_settings()` allowlist. Credential fields do not enter the summary.
1444: - Known credentials are only values configured or used by this application in this run; no collection of all environment variables and no credential registry file. Empty strings do not match; IF-21 defines the literal exact-substring matching contract; no long-string or provider-key heuristic.
1445: - If an allowlisted field contains a known credential as defined by IF-21, omit the entire affected field.
1446: - Endpoint preference: do not save/restore endpoints with userinfo, query, fragment (including an explicit empty separator), a known credential in host/path, or an unparseable form. Omit the item and require re-entry; do not save a masked pseudo-endpoint; do not strip query/fragment and save a different address; do not modify `.env` or migrate credentials.
1447: - Supported request errors: replace known credentials with a fixed marker (`***`); do not reattach unprocessed request/response objects, exception chains, or raw bodies; preserve safe error category and necessary diagnostics.
1448: - Handling failure: omit the field or use a fixed safe message; manifest handling failure skips the record and warns; no raw sensitive fallback; no hard exit.
1449: - Out of scope: model-generated report bodies, arbitrary third-party logs, raw debug/stream output, complete API return objects, historical files, recovery material, future outputs.
1450: - Existing `get_scrubbed` and `.env` 0600 behavior are retained as existing protections, not claimed as new results.
1451: 
1452: ### 9.2 SR-02 path confinement
1453: 
1454: - `run_id` must be a single safe path component: non-empty, no path separators, not `.`/`..`, not absolute, no injection form.
1455: - Ticker reuses `safe_ticker_component` (`dataflows/symbols.py:155`); no new symbol system.
1456: - The configured results root is the trusted starting point after resolution. Ownership is decided by components and resolved target, not string prefix (`/results-other` is not inside `/results`).
1457: - A root configured through a link uses the resolved actual location. No new approval or link policy.
1458: - For a not-yet-created manifest, check existing ancestors and controlled appended components; no check-then-use race guarantee.
1459: - Reject a candidate that resolves outside the root through an existing symbolic link. Do not reject a legitimate in-root link merely for containing a link.
1460: - Do not silently switch to the current working directory or another root.
1461: - No URL decoding/double-decoding beyond existing behavior.
1462: - `run_id` itself cannot be absolute; an existing absolute report reference may be read only if it resolves inside the root; out-of-root absolute references are rejected.
1463: - User-chosen report save directories outside the results root follow existing behavior; they are not automatically copied into or retrieved by FR-05, and history read authorization is not expanded.
1464: - Failure: FR-02 abandons the manifest write and warns; analysis continues. FR-05 illegal run_id is a parameter error; out-of-root reference is an invalid record; list skips bad records with warnings; direct read is rejected.
1465: - Threat model: local single-user controlled directory without malicious concurrent modification. Check-then-replace races, hard links, mounts, and all platform link mechanisms are not guaranteed.

1522: | Output consistency | CLI streaming sections, immediate files, final report, final state, state log, memory, return value; waiting/unchecked/failed labels |
1523: | Fault injection | Manifest running/terminal/serialization failures; save failure; corrupt manifest; missing report; invalid UTF-8; unsafe endpoint; symlink escape |

1556: - A requirement changes the final authority, entry-point set, or output consumers.

1561: - A requirement adds a unified context assembler, cross-role normalization, input budgets, automatic trimming/compression, or different role input obligations.

1563: - A security scope expansion is requested beyond SR-01/SR-02.
1564: - A deferred requirement (FR-06/FR-07/PR-01/CR-01) is activated.

1649: ## 15. Review checklist
1650: 
1651: - [ ] The fixed graph sequence Portfolio Manager → FR-04 → SB-01 → END is accepted.
1652: - [ ] Portfolio Manager writes only `model_proposal` as a nested `{rating, text}` object or `null`; SB-01 alone decides/generates `gate_status`, top-level `reasons`, `final_rating`, and `final_trade_decision`; unchanged pass-through/merge/save is allowed and is not a second authority.
1653: - [ ] Risk reasons remain in `portfolio_risk_result.reasons`; SB-01 reasons remain at the top level; no `present`, `gate_reasons`, or flattened risk object is required.
1654: - [ ] Missing/invalid formal output is an execution contract failure, not a consumer-generated REVIEW.
1655: - [ ] The availability snapshot is plumbing, not an approval authority.
1656: - [ ] Each of the 15 paths has one curated observation site; P-09/P-13 share one news executor/single-flight, P-03 observes each split indicator, and P-14/P-15 are observed at their direct prefetch calls.
1657: - [ ] No router, vendor, callback, monkeypatch, or middleware layer adds a second availability observation; defaults come from existing config/constants and early failures do not invent a valid query.
1658: - [ ] `AvailabilitySummary` has exactly the five agreed fields; the summarizer is the only completeness calculator, and consumers read one plain mapping without rebuilding it.
1659: - [ ] Necessary gaps are only a filter over non-available `necessary_items`; no duplicate `missing_necessary_items` field or second completeness state exists.
1660: - [ ] Observation, conservative unavailable, and query marks share one acceptance-order sequence; a later accepted update replaces an earlier one for that query, with no external-time ordering. Failure marks appear only as affected-query `unavailable`.
1661: - [ ] Pre-fetch parameter rejection creates only a private safe call-failure note, with no fake query/observation/sequence/FR-01 and no tracking error; it does not overwrite a valid result and appears as necessary-gap reason or supplementary limitation as appropriate.
1662: - [ ] Unlocatable/unrecordable observation loss sets private `availability_tracking_error`; later snapshots are `None`, not old complete data, while a single snapshot-construction failure is not sticky. A new run starts clean, and consumers see only missing/invalid summaries.
1663: - [ ] CLI creates the run before graph-object construction; `propagate()` creates it after invocation on an existing object; object construction is not an analysis run.
1664: - [ ] Resource cleanup belongs to the entry or resource wrapper; `RunContext.finish()` does not close streams or clients; the new flow acquires no checkpoint session.
1665: - [ ] FR-04 uses the field/threshold contract and exact rational comparisons; no float arithmetic, default Decimal context, or display rounding decides a check.
1666: - [ ] The risk result is one JSON-compatible object with decimal-string/null metrics; display formatting is local and never feeds back into status.
1667: - [ ] The deterministic risk area says only the listed caller scenario is checked and that other amounts/prices in the model proposal are not verified by this check.
1668: - [ ] Observation handling failure never replaces the fetch outcome or blocks shared publication; recordable failures stay at the query, and only unlocatable/unrecordable observation loss sets the private tracking error that makes later snapshots missing. No public permanent veto exists.
1669: - [ ] Title-only, placeholder, error text, or arbitrary numbers are not sufficient for `available`; minimum content rules are applied per P-02/P-04/P-09/P-10.
1670: - [ ] Every FR-03 path uses the verified per-method branch table; non-empty error text is not treated as `available`.
1671: - [ ] The first Bull call receives the research-start summary directly; later Bull/Bear and the Research Manager use the same stage summary; later observations do not refresh it or re-run research.
1672: - [ ] Existing role prompt assembly, full reports, identity/language, tool-message relationships, and structured-output/fallback paths remain; the context classes are logical, not a shared layer order.
1673: - [ ] Context budgets, compression thresholds, and compressed-constraint reinjection are deferred per ADR 001 D-10c and are not current behavior or acceptance; existing role inputs/client limits/error paths remain, and no unified budget/trim/reinjection flow is added.
1674: - [ ] Query identity excludes call path; completion observations and path associations are separate and ordered correctly.
1675: - [ ] `propagate()` never forces a report save, its return shape is unchanged, and returned final_state carries this analysis's terminal `data_availability_summary`.
1676: - [ ] Run-in reports use one entry-prepared terminal summary; independent `save_reports(final_state)` uses only that state, and the writer never reads active context, registry, summarizer, graph cache, research summary, or model text.
1677: - [ ] Markdown and HTML use the same report input; missing availability is disclosed as unavailable without a fabricated completeness value or SB-01 rerun; independent save does not modify an ended manifest.
1678: - [ ] One stats handler/collector is created per analysis and injected only through that graph execution's config; it is not model-constructor-bound, not stored on the reusable graph/model, and does not look up its run from context.
1679: - [ ] Duplicate callbacks are deduped by callback call ID; per-call usage drives null totals; graph-internal reflection is included, independent settlement is not; propagation gaps are treated as unverified with local config handoff, not a new router.
1680: - [ ] Manifest failure never changes the run outcome or formal result or masks the original error.
1681: - [ ] Report/final-state/new-memory failures use path-specific behavior and are not generalized to manifest best-effort.
1682: - [ ] FR-01/FR-03/FR-04/SB-01/manifest have independent component boundaries.
1683: - [ ] Intermediate proposal labels and formal waiting/failed states are accepted.
1684: - [ ] The new flow always executes fully from a new RunContext and initial state; it does not resume, read, or delete checkpoint data, and checkpoint-enabled configurations emit a no-resume notice.
1685: - [ ] SR-01 and SR-02 remain limited to the stated paths.
1686: - [ ] Deferred scope is not re-introduced.
1687: - [ ] All remaining open decisions are resolved or explicitly deferred by the human reviewer.

1: # D4 Bug Diary
2: 
3: - Document status: Reusable significant-bug record template with two registered records; this does not claim that no other bugs exist.
4: - Registered records: BUG-01 (contract-test placeholder path, Closed) and BUG-02 (reported macOS errno.EDEADLOCK failures, Open).
5: - Purpose: Preserve symptoms, reproduction, classification, root cause, fix history, regression evidence, and any exposed invariant or test gap for important bugs.
6: - Related records: [Review memo](review-memo.md) and [Debt register](debt-register.md).
7: 
8: This file does not claim that the project has no bugs. It records only bugs that have actually been observed and judged important. A failed test is not automatically an application defect; it may be a test defect, fixture problem, environment block, dependency gap, or expected behavior change requiring review.
9: 
10: ## 1. Recording rules
11: 
12: 1. Add a record only after a real symptom has been observed. Do not create illustrative bugs or prefill a root cause, fix, or result.
13: 2. Keep the lifecycle honest:
14:    - `Found`: symptom observed; cause not yet identified.
15:    - `Located`: root cause identified with evidence.
16:    - `Fix proposed`: a change is proposed but not implemented.
17:    - `Fixed`: a change exists, but independent re-verification is not complete.
18:    - `Re-verified`: the relevant regression test passed in the recorded environment.
19:    - `Closed`: re-verification is accepted and any follow-up is recorded.
20: 3. A proposal is not a fix. A code change without a recorded re-run is not `Re-verified`.
21: 4. Record actual versions, commands, inputs, and evidence. Do not invent timestamps, reviewers, commits, or pass results.
22: 5. Link the relevant D1 requirement/FC, D2 invariant/ADR, review memo, and debt record when known. If no relation is known, write `None known` rather than guessing.
23: 6. Preserve earlier findings when new evidence changes the diagnosis. Correct a prior statement explicitly instead of silently replacing history.
24: 7. Use a stable ID such as `BUG-<sequence>-<short-slug>`; use the same ID in review and debt records.
25: 
26: ## 2. Classification and impact guidance
27: 
28: Record a classification based on evidence. Common labels include behavior defect, test defect, fixture/data defect, environment or dependency failure, security or path-confinement defect, contract mismatch, and regression. Add a short impact statement covering affected entry points, outputs, state, reports, memory, or security boundaries.
29: 
30: A classification is not a severity threshold and does not create a new bug-acceptance rule. If the cause or impact is not yet established, say `Unknown` and keep the record open.
31:

1: # ADR 001 — Graph-Internal Final Check with Run-Scoped Governance
2: 
3: - Status: Proposed for human review
4: - Date: 2026-11-17
5: - Decision owners: Architecture review (human) with coding-agent analysis support
6: - Requirements baseline: `docs/req/requirements.yaml` version 1.48.0
7: - Related: [Architecture Blueprint](../../../architecture-blueprint.md), [Evaluation Table](../evaluation-table.md)
8: - Supersedes: the earlier proposal to run the final business check in a shared entry-boundary `RunFinalizer`
9: 
10: This ADR records the architecture selection and the ADD-R process. It intentionally separates:
11: 
12: - what the requirements require,
13: - what the existing code does,
14: - what this design selects,
15: - what remains an unapproved candidate or an unverified assumption.
16: 
17: No application code, test run, live model call, data-vendor call, measurement, or human approval is claimed.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. Context and problem
22: 
23: ### 1.1 Existing architecture
24: 
25: The repository is a LangGraph multi-agent analysis application. Both supported entry points eventually run the same graph:
26: 
27: - CLI: `cli/main.py` → `cli/run.py` → `TradingAgentsGraph` stream.
28: - Programmatic: `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()` → graph invoke.
29: 
30: The graph ends at the Portfolio Manager (`tradingagents/graph/setup.py:185`). The Portfolio Manager currently writes `final_rating` and `final_trade_decision` directly (`tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py:80-104`). Consumers then read or re-parse those fields:
31: 
32: - `tradingagents/agents/rating.py:106` `run_rating()` returns the field or parses the decision text.
33: - `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py:404` returns `(final_state, run_rating(final_state))`.
34: - CLI displays the rating and offers report saving (`cli/run.py:380`, `cli/run.py:426`).
35: - `record_decision()` writes the state log and memory (`trading_graph.py:358`).
36: - `write_report_tree()` renders the decision (`tradingagents/reporting.py:92`).
37: 
38: There is no native run manifest, no run lifecycle, no structured purchase-scenario risk check, no availability summary, no query reuse service, and no history lookup. Existing security helpers are partial: `get_scrubbed()` (`dataflows/net.py:6`) and `safe_ticker_component()` (`dataflows/symbols.py:155`).
39: 
40: ### 1.2 Requirements problem
41: 
42: The active requirements introduce a deterministic authority boundary:
43: 
44: - Portfolio Manager must produce only a model proposal.
45: - FR-04 must evaluate a caller-supplied structured purchase scenario.
46: - SB-01 must be the sole decision/generation authority for `final_rating` and `final_trade_decision`; downstream pass-through, merge, copy, and save of unchanged values are allowed.
47: - Consumers must not re-parse text into another formal rating.
48: - The normal completion path must not bypass SB-01.
49: - Checkpointing must not silently skip required checks.
50: - Intermediate proposal and formal output must be visibly separated.
51: - Manifest persistence is best-effort and must not change the run outcome or formal result. Report, final-state, and new-memory failures preserve existing exception/error behavior and may make the run `failed`; they never recompute or rewrite the formal result.
52: 
53: This is not a greenfield redesign. The graph, agents, vendors, reports, and memory remain usable; checkpoint code/tests remain in the repository outside the new flow.
54: 
55: ### 1.3 Design constraints
56: 
57: - Python >= 3.11, LangGraph, pytest, ruff.
58: - Two entries only.
59: - No model/data calls in FR-04/SB-01.
60: - No new database, index, background worker, recovery system, or generic scanner.
61: - Offline testability; the suite blocks network by default.
62: - No modification of requirements or governance configuration in this task.
63: - Module paths in this ADR are relative to `src/` after the approved layout migration; for example `cli/run.py` is `src/cli/run.py`.
64: 
65: ### 1.4 Requirement scope check
66: 
67: Independent count from `docs/req/requirements.yaml`:
68: 
69: | Scope | Requirements | Fit criteria |
70: |---|---|---|
71: | Active | 9 | 40 |
72: | Deferred | 4 | 15 |
73: | Total | 13 | 55 |
74: 
75: Active: FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04, FR-05, SB-01, INV-01, SR-01, SR-02.
76: Deferred: FR-06, FR-07, PR-01, CR-01.
77: 
78: This matches the expected scope. Deferred items are not designed as current behavior.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: ## 2. Decision summary
83: 
84: Select **graph-internal deterministic finalization with a run-scoped governance context and thin adapters**.
85: 
86: The graph becomes:
87: 
88: ```text
89: Existing analysis and debate
90:   → Portfolio Manager: model_proposal (advisory only)
91:   → Portfolio Risk Check node:
92:        AvailabilitySummarizer.snapshot(asset_type, enabled_analysts, analysis_context)
93:        PortfolioRiskEvaluator.evaluate()
94:        writes check-time data_availability_summary + portfolio_risk_result
95:   → after formal check: entry prepares terminal report summary into final/report state
96:   → Final Recommendation Check node:
97:        FinalRecommendationChecker.evaluate()
98:        writes gate_status, reasons,
99:               final_rating, final_trade_decision
100:   → END
101:   → CLI / propagate() consume formal fields only
102: ```
103: 
104: `RunContext` owns run identity, timing, status, stats, query reuse, availability registry, and manifest orchestration. It is not serialized into graph state or checkpoints.
105: 
106: The entry adapters do not perform a second business check. If an entry-boundary `RunFinalizer` exists, it coordinates entry-owned cleanup and terminalization; it does not create a second close path, and `RunContext.finish()` does not close resources.
107: 
108: ---
109: 
110: ## 3. ADD-R design process
111: 
112: ADD-R is used because the design retains and adjusts an existing architecture. Each round states its inputs, candidate concepts, decision, and remaining gap.
113: 
114: ### 3.1 Round 0 — Baseline, scope, and drivers
115: 
116: Inputs:
117: 
118: - Current source paths in Section 1.1.
119: - Active and deferred requirement counts.
120: - Baseline run `baseline-20261020-01` (old behavior only).
121: 
122: Activities:
123: 
124: - Confirm the two entry points and their divergence.
125: - Confirm the graph ends at the Portfolio Manager.
126: - Confirm the existing output surfaces: CLI, report, state log, memory, return value.
127: - Confirm the absence of the new governance components.
128: 
129: Decision D-00: retain the existing graph and add deterministic post-PM nodes; do not rewrite the analysis pipeline.
130: 
131: Remaining gap: no authority boundary, no run lifecycle, no data observation.
132: 
133: ### 3.2 Round 1 — Authority and intermediate/formal separation
134: 
135: Candidate concepts:
136: 
137: 1. Entry-boundary finalizer in both entries.
138: 2. Graph-internal final-check node.
139: 3. Independent post-graph service invoked by both entries.
140: 4. No new authority; keep Portfolio Manager fields and add display labels only.
141: 
142: Analysis:
143: 
144: - Entry-boundary finalizer duplicates the authority boundary and can diverge between CLI and `propagate()`. It also makes checkpoint behavior ambiguous.
145: - A graph node is part of every normal completion path and produces one state source for all consumers. Checkpoint compatibility can be handled explicitly.
146: - An independent service is a second orchestration path and risks bypass.
147: - Display-only labels do not satisfy SB-01/INV-01.
148: 
149: Decision D-01: graph-internal final check. Portfolio Manager writes only `model_proposal`. SB-01 alone decides and generates the formal values; entries, reducers, and writers may pass, merge, copy, or save them unchanged, but may not recompute, re-parse, replace, or fabricate them. Such pass-through is not a second authority.
150: 
151: Decision D-02: retain `model_proposal` separately as a nested `{rating, text}` object or `null`; inner values may be `null`, and no `present` boolean or fabricated proposal is added. Consumers never use it for formal fields. SB-01 produces a complete blocked/REVIEW for missing or invalid check inputs and a complete error/REVIEW for its own handled exceptions. A missing, wrong-type, empty-string, or whitespace-only model conclusion is an ordinary input-condition failure producing blocked/REVIEW, not an SB-01 internal error. A valid conclusion is preserved unchanged; whitespace stripping may be used only to test non-emptiness. A missing or invalid formal output after the graph is an execution contract failure, not a consumer-generated REVIEW and not a text-parsed rating. Top-level `reasons` belongs to SB-01; `portfolio_risk_result.reasons` stays scoped to FR-04 and is not flattened into the formal result.
152: 
153: Decision D-02a: define a lightweight shared `FormalResultContract` that validates the five top-level fields (`model_proposal`, `gate_status`, `reasons`, `final_rating`, `final_trade_decision`) and their types. It checks that `model_proposal` is a nested `{rating, text}` object or `null`, formal gate and rating sets are legal, passed has a five-tier formal rating, blocked/error has REVIEW, `final_trade_decision` is a non-whitespace string, `reasons` is a string list, and blocked/error has at least one actual reason. An illegal proposal rating is SB-01 input, not a contract failure. It returns the result unchanged or reports an execution contract failure. It does not recheck data or risk, call a model/data source, parse text, repair the result, or create a second business status. No `present` field, `gate_reasons` alias, signature, hash, source proof, persistent diagnostic system, or new module/public API is added.
154: 
155: Decision D-03: intermediate surfaces use explicit labels:
156: 
157: - “Original Model Proposal — Not Yet Checked” before the check.
158: - “Original Model Proposal — Did Not Pass Final Check” for blocked/error.
159: - Formal area waits, then displays SB-01 fields only.
160: 
161: Remaining gap: risk input and availability snapshot must reach the final node.
162: 
163: ### 3.3 Round 2 — Run lifecycle, manifest, and statistics
164: 
165: Candidate concepts:
166: 
167: 1. A process-global run singleton.
168: 2. A `RunContext` owned by the outermost entry and exposed through a context variable.
169: 3. A graph-managed manifest node.
170: 4. A separate manifest service with its own queue/process.
171: 
172: Analysis:
173: 
174: - A process-global singleton breaks parallel runs and tests.
175: - A graph node cannot own CLI save timing, resource close, or terminal status without mixing graph state and operational state.
176: - A separate service adds a new process/persistence system and violates the minimal constraint.
177: - A run-scoped context with a context variable matches the existing `run_config` pattern (`dataflows/config.py:44`) and supports concurrent analysts.
178: 
179: Decision D-04: `RunContext` creation is entry-specific and scoped to one analysis; it is not created by the object constructor. The CLI creates it after selection/config/basic validation and before graph-object construction. `propagate()` creates a new one after invocation, per-call validation, and effective-config resolution on an existing object. Object construction is analyzed separately from the analysis run. The context owns run_id, timers, status, the per-analysis stats handler/collector, reuse, availability, output references, and manifest orchestration, and is not serialized.
180: 
181: Decision D-04a: CLI object construction, client initialization, initial workflow compile, and per-run preparation are inside the run and its elapsed time. A CLI construction/client/compile/preparation failure is a post-start execution failure with a failed-manifest attempt and the original error preserved. Program object construction and idle time are outside the run; construction failure before `propagate()` creates no analysis run or manifest. The initial workflow compile is object construction for the CLI and pre-existing for the program entry; the new flow does not perform a checkpoint recompile.
182: 
183: Decision D-04b: the initial running manifest uses a shared config-summary projection over the effective configuration and selected analysts, following the existing `run_settings()` allowlist. It does not require a constructed graph, a second allowlist, extra graph construction, or a credential-policy expansion. The instance `run_settings()` reuses the projection.
184: 
185: Decision D-04c: resource cleanup has one owner per resource. The entry/execution scope coordinates necessary cleanup and summarizes the outcome; each wrapper releases only its own resource; `RunContext.finish()` receives the summarized outcome after cleanup attempts and records end time, stats snapshot, and terminal manifest. It does not close streams, call `end_checkpoint()`, delete checkpoint data, close clients, or repeat a close. Existing checkpoint storage, cleanup tools, and tests remain outside the new flow; the new flow does not acquire a checkpoint session or call success cleanup.
186: 
187: Decision D-05: manifest persistence is best-effort and atomic. Running and terminal writes are separate attempts. Manifest failure never changes the run outcome or formal result or masks the original error.
188: 
189: Decision D-05a: persistence handling is path-specific. Final-state JSON, new-memory append, and CLI-requested report failures preserve existing exception/error behavior and can make the run `failed`. Memory disabled or an existing same-day record is not a failure; `_memory_step()` settlement/reflection/read degradation stays degraded; an independent `save_reports()` after `propagate()` preserves that operation’s behavior and does not reopen the completed run. No transaction, rollback, or automatic repair is added.
190: 
191: Decision D-06: CLI save selection and save attempt are inside the run; display/browser are after the terminal attempt. `propagate()` does not force a save; a later save is outside the run.
192: 
193: Decision D-07: one per-analysis `RunStatsHandler` is created with the RunContext and directly owns its collector: a model-call record map, a tool-call ID set, one lock, and a snapshot method. The handler is merged into this graph invocation/stream's execution `callbacks` config, not bound to quick/deep model construction and not overwriting existing execution-config callbacks. Existing custom callbacks are preserved; only this analysis's handler is added once. Internal CLI delegation to propagate shares one analysis RunContext/handler, while an independent call gets a new one. The handler does not look up its run through active context and there is no global collector, event router, or dispatcher. The RunContext ContextVar remains for other lifecycle/reuse/availability purposes; only stats ownership is direct. Callback IDs deduplicate starts/ends and distinguish analysis `run_id`; they are never synthesized from prompt text, model name, or timestamp. If identity or association cannot be established, the affected totals become null with a safe warning rather than a fabricated count. Per-call end usage drives totals; error counts a call with incomplete usage; unfinished calls are incomplete; any incomplete/invalid usage makes both totals null. Zero calls is true zero. Callback/collector exceptions are isolated and do not change model/tool outcomes. Exact config propagation and usage extraction boundaries remain pending verification; local explicit config handoff is preferred if a boundary does not inherit.
194: 
195: Decision D-07a: reflection attribution follows execution. A graph Memory Log reflection belongs to this analysis when its call runs under this graph execution; an independent `settle_pending()` / `settle_all_pending()` call outside the graph is not attributed merely because it shares a model object. Prefer inherited execution config. If read-only evidence or later verification shows a specific nested boundary does not inherit, pass that same execution config locally into the graph node/reflection call. Do not attach a permanent collector, refactor settlement, add background-task association, cross-thread ownership, or recovery protocol.
196: 
197: Decision D-07b: callbacks count application-level model calls only. A structured-output request that actually starts counts once; a subsequent free-text fallback that actually starts counts again. A local structured-binding failure with no model request does not count. Parser, chain, and graph-node work does not add a model call, and a schema-tool declaration is not an external tool execution. 19: ## 3. Unique primary module ownership
20: 
21: Each logical architecture element must have exactly one primary owning module. Multiple related elements may share a module; an element does not require its own class, service, or file. Other modules may provide explicit call-site adapters or consume its outputs, but must not duplicate its decision logic.
22: 
23: The table below is a proposed implementation allocation for review, except that Round 1 created the C-08 module and Round 2 created the independent C-09 module. It is not a claim that other new files exist or an authorization to create them. Paths start at the project root; application paths use `src/`. A round may approve a different equally small allocation before implementation, provided the affected ownership table and D2 references remain consistent. Do not silently introduce a second owner.
